title: Functor infinity categories turn source pushouts into pullbacks
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories, full subcategories and mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe of small quasicategories and a larger universe for their collection $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. This infinity category has small colimits and is cartesian closed, with internal Hom the quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)$ including all coherent natural transformations. For a span of small infinity categories $B\leftarrow A\to D$ and its pushout $P=B\amalg_A D$ in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, restriction gives an equivalence of infinity categories
$$\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)}\operatorname{Fun}(D,E)$$
for every infinity category $E$ in a sufficiently large universe. The right side is the pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$: its objects consist of functors on $B,D$ and a coherent equivalence between their restrictions to $A$; its transformations include noninvertible transformations with their coherent compatibility on $A$. These equivalences are natural in maps of spans and in $E$, and commute with composition of transformations. In particular this assertion is about the whole functor infinity category, not just its core.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, especially the internal Hom preceding Proposition 3.1.3.3; Proposition 3.1.4.2 and Corollary 3.1.4.3 for the cartesian model structure over a point; Corollary 4.2.4.8 for small colimits of the associated infinity category. The displayed internal-Hom pushout formula is an agent-formulated consequence of cartesian closedness and the mapping-space universal property. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical formula.
